title: Identification and Inference for Causal Effects in Extremes under General Conditions
abstract: arXiv:2608.22957v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Understanding the propagation of extreme events is important in many economic and environmental applications, yet most econometric methods for causal inference focus on average effects rather than tail behavior. This paper studies the identification of causal relations in extremes and derives resulting estimators and their asymptotic inference. As measure of causal dependence between extreme realizations of variables, we analyze the asymptotic behavior of the Causal Tail Coefficient (CTC) within a linear structural causal model with heavy-tailed regularly varying innovations. In contrast to the existing literature, we allow the variables in the system to exhibit heterogeneous tail indices and consider the presence of potentially heavy-tailed confounders. We derive theoretical results assessing the limiting behavior of the CTC under these conditions and show how differences in tail behavior can help to reach identification of the causal

translated_title: 一般条件下极端事件因果效应的识别与推断
translated_abstract: 摘要：理解极端事件的传播在许多经济和环境应用中非常重要，但大多数计量经济学因果推断方法侧重于平均效应，而非尾部行为。本文研究了极端情况下因果关系的识别，并推导出相应的估计量及其渐近推断。作为变量极端实现之间因果依赖的度量，我们在一个具有重尾正则变化创新的线性结构因果模型中分析了因果尾部系数（CTC）的渐近行为。与现有文献相比，我们允许系统中的变量表现出异质尾部指数，并考虑潜在重尾混淆变量的存在。我们推导了理论结果，评估了在这些条件下CTC的极限行为，并展示了尾部行为的差异如何有助于实现因果识别。
tldr: 本文在允许异质尾部指数和潜在重尾混淆变量的一般条件下，研究了极端事件中因果关系的识别，并推导了因果尾部系数的渐近推断方法。
en_tdlr: This paper studies causal identification in extremes under general conditions with heterogeneous tail indices and potentially heavy-tailed confounders, deriving asymptotic inference for the Causal Tail Coefficient.
